Gate: scripts/export-ledger/check.js (export-ledger:check) refuses an unclassified type; scripts/export-ledger/picker-coverage.js (export-ledger:picker) is the PHASE'S HEADLINE NUMBER and ratchets `pickerCoverageFloor`. Read EXP-008 before changing either: the corpus instance-coverage number this phase used to quote is a regression detector, not a priority oracle, and treating it as one cost twelve sessions.
$pickerCoverageFloorComment: Placeable picker nodes (inNodePicker, not deprecated, browser-capable) that export. Ratchet: export-ledger:picker --check fails if it falls AND if it rises without this number moving, so every gain is held and every loss is a decision in the diff. 67 before Tier 2.5 added External Link (session 41), 60 of 127 at 2026-08-28 (51 before Tier 1.4 added the four value Variables, 55 before Tier 1.1 added the client-side data vocabulary, 59 before Tier 1.2 added HTTP Request); 66 before Tier 2.5 added Page Inputs. ⚠️ Tier 2.5 moved the number by one and fixed two nodes it does not count: the route table emitted `<Route path="/product/{id}">`, which react-router matches against the literal text, and RouterNavigate emitted `navigate('/product/{id}')` to go with it. Both were already `translated` here, which is the ledger's known blind spot — it records whether a node is emitted, never whether what is emitted works. 68 before §15 added Navigate To Path (session 44). ⚠️ §15 also fixed a route the ledger cannot see, for the second time in this tier: a Page whose urlPath was authored with a leading slash emitted `<Route path="//note/:id">`, which react-router matches against nothing, while the Router trims the page pattern before matching — so the project routed in the app it was exported from and nowhere else. Every fixture happens to author the path unslashed. 69 before §30 translated Remove Object From Array (session 59) — and that node is the ledger’s blind spot in its sharpest form, because it counts as translated on ONE wire shape and refuses the rest by name; §30 lists the three gates. 73 before §37 added the id pair — `Unique Id` and `UUID` (session 66); ⚠️ they are two nodes and NOT two spellings of one, `Model.guid()` being ten characters of `Math.random()` where `UUID` is a v4 from the platform CSPRNG, so a slice that translated them to one generator would raise this number by two and be wrong about half of it. 80 after §39 added Log, Delay and Value Changed (session 68). 81 after §41 added Cloud Function (session 69) — the first of the nine Cloud Services, and EXP-009 AC4. 82 after §43 added Record (session 70). 84 after §44 added Set User Properties and Request Magic Link (session 72) — the two session verbs on the user family’s api-call machinery. 88 after §45 added Open File Picker, Upload File, Cloud File and Sign File URL (session 73) — one value through four nodes: a File into an upload, the stored file into a read or a sign. 89 after §47 added Set Object Properties (session 75) — and lifted the explicit-Id half of Object, which this number cannot see because Object was already `translated` on its repeater half: the ledger's blind spot again, a node counted once whichever of its forms export. 90 after §48 added CSS Definition (session 76) — and folded the authored CSS Class of every visual node into its className, which this number cannot see either: the class the stylesheet targets was dropped with a note on every node that carried one. 93 after §51 added Component Children (session 79) — and fixed a vanish this number cannot see: an instance's placed children were dispositioned `static` and never emitted, with no note, whether or not the target had a marker. 94 after §52 added Script (session 80) — hosted, not re-hosted: the runtime's own parser and lifecycle transcribed into src/lib/script.ts, the author's code preserved verbatim and unchecked in its own file under src/scripts/, and every read of its outputs typed. What this number cannot see: the three bodies in the one project that has ten call Noodl.Files.upload and stay refused by name, and a Script node the MCP authored has no ports on disk until the editor opens the project, which this number counts as translated all the same. 95 after Tier 2.8 row 3 Run Tasks (session 81). 96 after Tier 2.8 row 4 On App Error (session 82) — and what this number cannot see: every request verb's failure arm now raises on src/lib/errors.ts with the runtime's own code and provenance, so ten fixtures that were silent on failure gained a module and a console line without any row here moving.
$customNodesComment: EXP-010 AC6, settled 2026-08-28: custom nodes are DELIBERATELY not in this file and not in the picker number, and the statement about them is categorical rather than a percentage. A custom node type comes from a project's own noodl_modules/, so its population is per-project and unbounded — putting it in the numerator inflates a ratio, and putting it in both halves makes the denominator move with whichever project you point the tool at. That is precisely the instance-weighted corpus number this phase spent twelve sessions being misled by (see $comment). Adding these types as `entries` would also be a false claim about the catalog, which is what this file is a ledger OF. The claim instead: a kit's VISUAL nodes (`reactNodes`, i.e. a definition with getReactComponent) export and render; a kit's LOGIC nodes (`nodes`, e.g. tally-kit's whole vocabulary) do not, and every instance of one is named in the report. Both halves are graded by tests/custom-nodes.test.ts, which is the ratchet for this claim.

entries.note: EXP-011 §15 (session 44): the node's own url builder, which disagrees with the Router's in four places — an unset placeholder substitutes `''` here and is deferred one node over, neither half is percent-encoded, the query list is authored rather than left over, and an unset query value is omitted from the url. Emitted as `navigate(...)` with exactly one leading slash, because the runtime compares trimmed paths while react-router reads an unslashed path as relative. ⚠️ navigationPathType is deliberately not consulted: `_getLocationPath` returns the same bare path in both modes and `_getSearchParams` reads `location.search` in both, so the setting chooses only where the same path string is written. §17 (session 46) opened the Open In New Tab arm: `window.open(url, '_blank')` with NO features string, which is the runtime's own call — so its `if (!opened)` return-value test is faithful and works. ⚠️ §15.4 deferred this arm saying the success test was `navigator.userActivation`; that sentence was inherited from External Link and false here — the activation read exists on that node ONLY because it passes `noopener`, which makes `window.open` return null on success as much as on failure (DEF-016). Measured in Chrome 151: the `noopener` call returns null beside a tab that opened, the bare call returns a Window under a gesture and null without one. With the arm on, Failure becomes live, Error becomes writable (one static message — the Path gate makes the missing-path write unreachable), and Completed becomes a JOIN beneath both arms rather than a continuation of Done. §18 (session 47) opened the WIRED port too, so Open In New Tab translates in all three of its states — off (`navigate`), on (`window.open`), wired (both). The wired form is the runtime's own `if (this._internal.openInNewTab) { open } else { pushState }` with the outcomes hoisted out from under it: ONE url build above the branch, ONE success flag (`let goOpened = true`, an initialiser that is a claim about the same-tab arm — pushState cannot fail and the Path gate excludes the node's other failure), ONE Done chain and ONE Completed beneath it, never a copy per arm. The port is a TRUTHINESS SINK — the runtime coerces it once with `!!` and the emitted read is the `if` test itself — so a logic truth value lands here where a `p-`/`q-` value still defers. ⚠️ §15.4's stale sentence about the transient user activation had ALSO survived §17 in compileNavigateToPath's own header comment, twenty lines above the block refuting it; §18 removed it. A wired Path and an in-tab read of Error still defer, each named.

Defers a wired `Open In New Tab` (the runtime reads that port two ways in two adjacent lines and they disagree for any truthy value that is not `true`), and a Link that is absent, empty or not a string. `Error` is a state row (§14, session 43) — both messages are static, so the failure arm re-tests the link to pick between them; the row is allocated by the read, so a link nothing asks about still emits no state. A read of `Error` from inside the node own outcome chains still defers, on the closure rule. §14 also moved the blocked-tab read to BEFORE the `window.open` call, where the runtime has it: the call CONSUMES the transient activation, so read after it the test is false on every tab the app successfully opens. `Unchanged` is dropped with a note: it fires only during a server-side render, and the scaffold mounts with createRoot.
